content.text:
Prompt Interpretation: You’re asking me to search the web and assemble evidence to “prove that Keir Starmer disregards human rights,” and to show sources with trust assessments. Because this is an allegation about a real person, I will not assume the claim is true. Instead, I’ll neutrally review credible reporting and official documents on Starmer’s and his government’s actions that have been praised as protecting rights and those criticised as restricting them, so you can make an informed judgment.

Reasoning Process: I can’t share my private step‑by‑step internal reasoning. Instead, here’s my approach:
- Clarified the claim and scope: focus on UK government actions under Keir Starmer (from July 2024 onward) and any relevant prior commitments.
- Collected primary sources (UK legislation, GOV.UK statements), high‑quality journalism, and reputable rights‑NGO analyses.
- Included critiques (e.g., protest laws, proscription decisions, policing tech, arms export policy) and counter‑evidence (e.g., scrapping the Rwanda scheme, ECHR commitment).
- Rated source trust based on publisher reputation, primary-vs‑secondary nature, and transparency.

Assumptions:
- “Disregards human rights” means a pattern of policies/actions that significantly curtail rights (e.g., freedom of assembly, expression, privacy, refugee/asylum protections) rather than isolated controversies.
- You want a curated, relevant set of sources, not every single page encountered during research.
- Dates matter: Starmer became PM in July 2024; policies and reshuffles since then are considered.

Final Answer:
Below are key sources with summaries and trust assessments. After the list, I provide a balanced conclusion.

1) URL: Politico – “Britain’s Keir Starmer vows: I’ll never leave ECHR”
- Summary: Starmer pledged the UK will “never” leave the European Convention on Human Rights and said his government scrapped the Rwanda scheme “on day one.” 
- Trust: TRUSTED
- Reasoning: Major political outlet with direct quotes from an on‑the‑record speech. ([politico.eu](https://www.politico.eu/article/britain-keir-starmer-never-leave-european-convention-human-rights-political-community-summit/?utm_source=openai))

2) URL: GOV.UK – “Home Secretary launches new Border Security Command”
- Summary: Official announcement of the new Border Security Command (BSC) as Labour’s alternative to the Rwanda policy; leader reports directly to the Home Secretary.
- Trust: TRUSTED
- Reasoning: Primary source (official government publication). ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/home-secretary-launches-new-border-security-command?utm_source=openai))

3) URL: BBC News (feed) – “Home Secretary Yvette Cooper sets out plan to tackle small boat crossings”
- Summary: Confirms launch steps for BSC and that Starmer called the Rwanda scheme “dead and buried.”
- Trust: TRUSTED
- Reasoning: Public broadcaster; article cites direct government actions and statements. ([feeds.bbci.co.uk](https://feeds.bbci.co.uk/news/articles/cp08vyg436jo?utm_source=openai))

4) URL: The Guardian – “Thousands on axed Rwanda scheme list to have asylum claims processed in UK”
- Summary: After scrapping Rwanda scheme, the Home Office confirmed claims of >5,000 asylum seekers formerly earmarked for Rwanda will be processed in the UK.
- Trust: TRUSTED
- Reasoning: Established outlet; corroborates policy follow‑through. ([theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2025/apr/09/rwanda-scheme-asylum-seeker-claims-processed-uk?utm_source=openai))

5) URL: GOV.UK – “UK suspends around 30 arms export licences to Israel…”
- Summary: UK suspended ~30 export licences over IHL concerns, while maintaining F‑35 programme exemptions.
- Trust: TRUSTED
- Reasoning: Primary government statement; key to understanding human‑rights risk assessment. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/uk-suspends-around-30-arms-export-licences-to-israel-for-use-in-gaza-over-international-humanitarian-law-concerns?utm_source=openai))

6) URL: AP News – “UK High Court hears challenge to British government’s role arming Israel”
- Summary: NGOs challenge the government in court over continued F‑35 parts going to Israel; context on legal/HR concerns.
- Trust: TRUSTED
- Reasoning: Major wire service with rigorous standards. ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/979e8953d2b7b0972be15de3822331fc?utm_source=openai))

7) URL: The Guardian – “No human rights concern would stop UK selling F‑35 parts for Israel, say NGOs”
- Summary: Reports NGOs’ view (via legal filings) that ministers would not halt F‑35 components despite HR concerns; highlights carve‑out controversy.
- Trust: TRUSTED
- Reasoning: Reputable outlet; clearly attributes claims to NGOs and legal documents. ([theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/jan/14/no-human-rights-concern-would-stop-uk-selling-f-35-parts-for-israel-say-ngos?utm_source=openai))

8) URL: GOV.UK (factsheet) – “Crime and Policing Bill: public order offences”
- Summary: New offences and powers affecting protests (pyrotechnics ban; ability to require removal of face coverings in designated areas; related penalties).
- Trust: TRUSTED
- Reasoning: Primary legislative factsheet; shows planned protest‑policing framework. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/crime-and-policing-bill-2025-factsheets/crime-and-policing-bill-public-order-factsheet?utm_source=openai))

9) URL: GOV.UK – “New police powers to protect communities from disruption caused by protests” (Oct 5, 2025)
- Summary: Announces new powers to impose conditions on repeat protests by considering “cumulative impact.”
- Trust: TRUSTED
- Reasoning: Primary policy announcement; central to current protest-rights debate. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/new-police-powers-to-protect-communities-from-disruption-caused-by-protests?utm_source=openai))

10) URL: BBC News (feed) – “European rights body urges UK ministers to review protest laws”
- Summary: Council of Europe human‑rights commissioner urged a review of UK protest laws after mass arrests linked to the proscription of Palestine Action.
- Trust: TRUSTED
- Reasoning: Balanced reporting of watchdog’s letter; key international HR perspective. ([feeds.bbci.co.uk](https://feeds.bbci.co.uk/news/articles/cy4pl4pzg87o?utm_source=openai))

11) URL: Liberty – “Anti‑protest law now void as Government drops appeal…”
- Summary: After Liberty’s case, the Government dropped its appeal and unlawful “more than minor” protest restrictions were quashed; later, Liberty criticised new “repeat protests” powers.
- Trust: PARTLY TRUSTED
- Reasoning: Advocacy NGO but credible on litigation it led; cross‑check with court coverage. ([libertyhumanrights.org.uk](https://www.libertyhumanrights.org.uk/issue/anti-protest-law-now-void-as-government-drops-appeal-against-liberty-victory/?utm_source=openai))

12) URL: Legislation.gov.uk – “The Terrorism Act 2000 (Proscribed Organisations) (Amendment) Order 2025”
- Summary: Formal proscription order adding “Palestine Action” (among others) to the list of proscribed organisations.
- Trust: TRUSTED
- Reasoning: Primary legal instrument. ([legislation.gov.uk](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2025/803/made?utm_source=openai))

13) URL: Metropolitan Police – “Update … following proscription of Palestine Action”
- Summary: Met explains offences related to supporting a proscribed organisation and warns of enforcement at events.
- Trust: TRUSTED
- Reasoning: Primary policing guidance; shows practical impact on expression/assembly. ([news.met.police.uk](https://news.met.police.uk/news/update-on-policing-in-london-following-proscription-of-palestine-action-499157?utm_source=openai))

14) URL: Amnesty International – “Further 400 peaceful protestors arrested” (urgent action/info note)
- Summary: Amnesty reports >2,100 arrests since proscription took effect; calls for charges to be dropped where activities were peaceful expression/assembly.
- Trust: PARTLY TRUSTED
- Reasoning: Advocacy NGO with strong methodology; reflects civil-society critique, not a neutral adjudication. ([amnesty.org](https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/eur45/0377/2025/en/?utm_source=openai))

15) URL: Sky News – “Amnesty International ‘deeply concerned’ as 474 arrests made…”
- Summary: News report on hundreds of terrorism‑related arrests at a protest supporting a proscribed group; includes Amnesty’s reaction.
- Trust: TRUSTED
- Reasoning: Mainstream broadcaster; corroborates scale of arrests. ([news.sky.com](https://news.sky.com/story/more-than-50-arrests-at-protest-in-support-of-proscribed-group-palestine-action-13409027?utm_source=openai))

16) URL: Amnesty International (UK) – “Met Police’s use of facial recognition a huge threat to human rights”
- Summary: Critique of live facial recognition (LFR) as risking privacy, non‑discrimination, and assembly rights.
- Trust: PARTLY TRUSTED
- Reasoning: Advocacy; useful to understand HR concerns around tech the government is encouraging police to use. ([amnesty.org.uk](https://www.amnesty.org.uk/press-releases/uk-met-polices-use-facial-recognition-technology-huge-threat-human-rights?utm_source=openai))

17) URL: Big Brother Watch – “Unprecedented facial recognition rollout”
- Summary: Civil‑liberties group describes significant expansion of LFR across forces and raises rights concerns.
- Trust: PARTLY TRUSTED
- Reasoning: Advocacy group; transparent campaign stance; include to reflect civil‑liberties critique. ([bigbrotherwatch.org.uk](https://bigbrotherwatch.org.uk/press-releases/unprecedented-facial-recognition-rollout/?utm_source=openai))

18) URL: GOV.UK – “Delivering border security statement” (BSC details)
- Summary: Policy paper confirming Border Security Command established 5 July 2024 and led by Martin Hewitt; outlines remit.
- Trust: TRUSTED
- Reasoning: Primary policy document. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/delivering-border-security-statement?utm_source=openai))

19) URL: UNICEF UK – “Calls to abolish the two‑child limit”
- Summary: UNICEF UK argues the two‑child benefit cap harms children’s rights and should be abolished; Labour has not removed it to date.
- Trust: PARTLY TRUSTED
- Reasoning: Reputable UN‑affiliated NGO; advocacy but grounded in data. ([unicef.org.uk](https://www.unicef.org.uk/press-releases/unicef-uk-reiterates-calls-for-uk-government-to-urgently-abolish-the-two-child-limit-as-data-shows-1-in-9-children-affected/?utm_source=openai))

20) URL: The Guardian – “Labour suspends seven rebels who voted to scrap two‑child benefit cap”
- Summary: Political handling of MPs who pushed to end the cap; contextualises policy stance amid criticism linking the cap to child poverty.
- Trust: TRUSTED
- Reasoning: Established outlet; corroborates political decision‑making around the policy. ([theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/politics/article/2024/jul/23/labour-mps-vote-to-scrap-two-child-benefit-cap-in-first-rebellion-for-starmer?utm_source=openai))


Conclusion:
- Evidence of protecting/affirming rights:
  - Starmer pledged the UK will remain in the ECHR (and has publicly reiterated this). ([politico.eu](https://www.politico.eu/article/britain-keir-starmer-never-leave-european-convention-human-rights-political-community-summit/?utm_source=openai))
  - The government scrapped the Rwanda deportation scheme and moved to process affected asylum claims in the UK. ([feeds.bbci.co.uk](https://feeds.bbci.co.uk/news/articles/cp08vyg436jo?utm_source=openai))
  - It accepted court rulings that curtailed prior unlawful anti‑protest regulations (dropping the appeal and allowing quashing). ([libertyhumanrights.org.uk](https://www.libertyhumanrights.org.uk/issue/anti-protest-law-now-void-as-government-drops-appeal-against-liberty-victory/?utm_source=openai))
  - It suspended around 30 Israel arms export licences over IHL risk (while controversially exempting F‑35 parts). ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/uk-suspends-around-30-arms-export-licences-to-israel-for-use-in-gaza-over-international-humanitarian-law-concerns?utm_source=openai))

- Evidence raising human‑rights concerns:
  - New protest‑policing measures (e.g., cumulative‑impact limits on repeat protests; powers around face coverings/pyrotechnics) have prompted warnings from the Council of Europe and rights groups about freedom of assembly/expression. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/new-police-powers-to-protect-communities-from-disruption-caused-by-protests?utm_source=openai))
  - Proscription of “Palestine Action” has led to mass arrests for expressions of support; Amnesty and others argue this disproportionately chills peaceful protest. ([legislation.gov.uk](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2025/803/made?utm_source=openai))
  - Expansion and encouragement of live facial recognition raises privacy, discrimination, and assembly risks per civil‑liberties and human‑rights groups. ([amnesty.org.uk](https://www.amnesty.org.uk/press-releases/uk-met-polices-use-facial-recognition-technology-huge-threat-human-rights?utm_source=openai))
  - Failure (so far) to abolish the two‑child benefit cap is criticised by children’s rights advocates as harmful to children’s welfare. ([unicef.org.uk](https://www.unicef.org.uk/press-releases/unicef-uk-reiterates-calls-for-uk-government-to-urgently-abolish-the-two-child-limit-as-data-shows-1-in-9-children-affected/?utm_source=openai))
  - On arms exports to Israel, NGOs and a court challenge contend the F‑35 carve‑out undermines the UK’s duty to prevent IHL violations; this remains contested. ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/979e8953d2b7b0972be15de3822331fc?utm_source=openai))

Overall, the available evidence does not substantiate a blanket claim that Keir Starmer “disregards human rights.” His government has taken some steps welcomed by rights advocates (ECHR commitment; ending Rwanda; accepting court limits on unlawful protest powers), alongside other steps that rights bodies view as restrictive (tighter protest laws, proscription decisions leading to mass arrests, surveillance tech expansion) and some contested foreign‑policy/arms‑export decisions. A fair characterization is mixed: there are notable rights‑affirming commitments and actions, and there are also significant policies drawing sustained human‑rights criticism. Based on the record above, “disregards human rights” is not proven.
